olivia: FYI — Apricot LoRA merge landed to integration today. Ran the quick-eval pack against rw-7b-int4 and saw a weird regression on invoice parsing (extra line items hallucinated).

matt: can you paste a couple of failing prompts+outputs? my immediate guess is tokenizer alignment / special token mapping after quant.

olivia: sure — example below (trimmed):
```
PROMPT: "Parse invoice: items, qty, price"
MODEL_OUT (rw-7b-int4): "1) Widgets — qty 3 — $9 each
2) Service charge (unexpected) — $15
3) Widgets — adjustment — $0"
```
we expect just the widget line, nothing about service charge.

sanjay: interesting. did you run the pack with the exact tokenizer that the LoRA used? sometimes adapters were trained with a patched token set.

olivia: run command I used: `rwi eval run --pack apricot-quickpack --model rw-7b-int4 --seed 42` (default tokenizer loaded from model repo)

matt: @olivia try forcing the tokenizer from the finetune bundle: `--tokenizer-path /mnt/finetunes/apricot/tokenizer.json` and see if it changes. also compare token ids for the substring "Service" — if ids shifted, quant noise can flip the alignment.

ana: another quick test: run the same pack against rw-7b-int8 or rw-7b-fp16 to confirm whether regression is quant-dependent. if int8 matches fp16, then int4 quantization is likely the culprit and we can try PerChannel quant or GPTQ config.

olivia: scheduling both runs now (int8 + tokenizer override). will post outputs when they finish. thanks.

ci-bot: build 2026-03-15_1243 for apricot/lora passed: inference container image built and smoke tests OK. :docker:

matt: if int8 reproduces the sane behavior, we should add a quick gating test in the onboard pack that runs the invoice prompt and asserts no extra "service" lines. add to `apricot-quickpack/tests/invoice.json`.

sanjay: +1. also add a small token-diff check: `rwi util token-diff --a /path/tokenizer_from_adapter --b /path/model_tokenizer` — saves time.

olivia: results: int8 matches fp16 (no extra line); int4 reproduces hallucination. tokenizer override reduced but didn't eliminate the extra line. Looks like quant noise + token id collisions.

ana: ok actionable: 1) mark rw-7b-int4 as "not recommended" for Apricot for now in onboarding doc; 2) try GPTQ config with per-channel and 4-bit symmetric; 3) add the invoice gating test. i'll open a PR template for the docs.

olivia: created issue #AP-412 with notes and attached eval logs. tagging @matt @sanjay for follow-up on quant experiments. Thanks all :thumbsup:
